polityAgreements.terms: Each Etruscan city made its own peace with Rome after 280, and sends men to Rome's wars.
Allied since Camerinum's treaty of 310: men for Rome's wars, no war or peace of their own.
Allied since 299: men for Rome's wars, no war or peace of their own.
Allied since 304: the Marsi, Paeligni, Marrucini and Vestini send men to Rome's wars.
Bound to Rome after defeat in 290 and again in 272: men for Rome's wars, no war or peace of their own.
Bound to Rome after defeat in 272: men for Rome's wars, no war or peace of their own.
Bound to Rome after defeat in 272, when they gave up half the Sila forest.
Tarentum surrendered in 272 and keeps its own laws under a Roman garrison; Arpi and the Daunians have been allies since 326. All send men and ships to Rome's wars.
Rome means to retake Rhegium from the garrison that seized it and killed its citizens.
polityAgreements.endedReason: Campanian legion of Rhegium accepted "Terms for ending the war at Rhegium".

polityAgreements.terms: Rome offers peace only upon the Campanian garrison's surrender of Rhegium and its arms, and the delivery of those responsible for the killing of the city's citizens for Roman judgment.

Messana asks Rome to consider protection against Syracuse while preserving the city's self-rule and local laws. We seek a prompt hearing and assistance sufficient to deter an attack; the people of Messana must be heard before any settlement of their status.
Open war following Rome's crossing to Messana and Carthage's opposition to Roman presence at the strait.

Rome demands that Syracuse cease its hostilities against Messana. Continued attacks will be treated as an invitation to open war. Rome has undertaken to protect Messana; this warning does not waive the city's self-rule or its right to be heard.

diplomacy.terms: Submit Messana to Syracusan authority and spare the island a wider war. Hieron will hear terms that secure Syracuse and preserve the lives of the city’s inhabitants.
diplomacy.subject: Submission of Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Messana will not submit to Syracusan authority. We will discuss terms that preserve the city's self-rule and the lives of its inhabitants; send an envoy before force makes such terms impossible.

diplomacy.terms: Rome offers peace only upon the Campanian garrison's surrender of Rhegium and its arms, and the delivery of those responsible for the killing of the city's citizens for Roman judgment.
diplomacy.subject: Terms for ending the war at Rhegium
diplomacy.answerText: I accept Rome’s terms. Rhegium and its arms are yielded, and those responsible for the killings will be delivered for Roman judgment.

diplomacy.terms: Messana will not submit to Syracusan authority. We will discuss terms that preserve the city's self-rule and the lives of its inhabitants; send an envoy before force makes such terms impossible.
diplomacy.subject: Terms for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: I will hear your envoy and discuss terms that preserve the lives of Messana’s people and its local laws. Syracuse cannot accept a settlement that leaves the city beyond our authority.

diplomacy.terms: Syracuse seeks to settle its dispute with the Mamertines at Messana. Carthage has no cause to fear a move against its western possessions or sea lanes. I urge Carthage to remain neutral while Syracuse pursues this matter.
diplomacy.subject: Syracuse and the strait
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage will remain neutral for now, provided Syracuse consults us before any move that threatens the strait or our western possessions. Send an envoy so we can agree on what such consultation requires.

diplomacy.terms: Send an envoy to Syracuse to discuss local self-rule, the safety of Messana’s inhabitants, and the city’s place under Syracusan authority. I will hear your proposals before deciding on force.
diplomacy.subject: An envoy to discuss Messana’s terms
diplomacy.answerText: I will send an envoy to discuss terms. Messana’s safety and local laws must be heard, and I will not surrender the city’s self-rule before the people’s case is put.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage will remain neutral for now. Before any move that could threaten the strait or our western possessions, Syracuse must consult Carthage. Send an envoy so we can agree on the scope of that consultation.
diplomacy.subject: Consultation before any move at Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse accepts consultation before action affecting the strait or your western possessions. We will send an envoy to settle its scope; our right to resolve the dispute with Messana remains.

diplomacy.terms: Surrender and the only punishmenet you shall face is you and your men 10 years in a punitive legion for rome under my command. After these 10 years you shall become citizens again
diplomacy.subject: Surrender and the only punishmenet you shall face is you and your men 10 years…
diplomacy.answerText: I accept your terms. I and my men will surrender Rhegium and its arms, and those responsible for the killings will be delivered for Roman judgment. We will serve ten years in the punitive legion under your command, then become citizens again.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage is prepared to remain neutral for now. Before further action at Messana that could affect the strait or Carthaginian western possessions, consult Carthage as proposed. This protects our interests while avoiding a wider conflict.
diplomacy.subject: Consultation over Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse accepts consultation with Carthage before further action affecting the strait or your western possessions. We will settle its scope by envoy.

diplomacy.terms: Syracuse will consult Carthage before further action at Messana that could affect the strait or Carthaginian western possessions. This consultation does not surrender Syracuse’s right to settle its dispute with the Mamertines.
diplomacy.subject: Consultation before action at Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage accepts consultation before action affecting the strait or its western possessions. Let envoys settle the notice and procedure; Carthage remains neutral for now.

diplomacy.terms: I will consult Carthage before any move that threatens the strait or your western possessions. Let us agree by envoys what notice and consultation require; meanwhile I will hear Mettius’s envoy before deciding on force.
diplomacy.subject: Consultation before action at Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage accepts consultation before action affecting the strait or its western possessions. Let envoys settle the notice and procedure; Carthage remains neutral for now.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage will send an envoy to agree with Syracuse on what notice and consultation require before action affecting the strait or Carthaginian western possessions. Carthage remains neutral while these discussions proceed.
diplomacy.subject: Carthaginian envoys on consultation
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse accepts consultation by envoys. Let us settle clear notice before any action affecting the strait or Carthaginian western possessions; Syracuse will remain within that understanding while the talks proceed.

diplomacy.terms: I have sent an envoy to Syracuse to agree on notice and consultation before action affecting the strait or Carthaginian western possessions. Carthage will remain neutral for now while we settle this procedure.
diplomacy.subject: Envoy to settle consultation at the strait
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse accepts Carthage's neutrality while our envoys settle notice and consultation. I will name a representative and agree on a meeting place.

diplomacy.terms: Messana asks Rome to consider protection against Syracuse while preserving the city's self-rule and local laws. We seek a prompt hearing and assistance sufficient to deter an attack; the people of Messana must be heard before any settlement of their status.
diplomacy.subject: Protection for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: We accept Messena's protectorate. We shall defend Messena whenever they call for us, in exchange we shall receive money and manpower as well as your participation in any war Rome is in

diplomacy.terms: I will receive your envoy and hear Messana’s terms for its safety and self-rule. Send him to Syracuse; the discussion will precede any decision about the city.
diplomacy.subject: Audience on Messana’s terms
diplomacy.answerText: I accept the audience. Hear Messana's terms for safety and self-rule before deciding the city's future.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage will send an envoy to settle notice and procedure for consultation before action affecting the strait or our western possessions. Please name your representatives and a meeting place. Our neutrality remains in force while these discussions proceed.
diplomacy.subject: Carthaginian envoy on consultation at Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse accepts consultation with Carthage before action affecting the strait or its western possessions. Our envoy will settle notice and procedure; Syracuse retains its right to resolve the Mamertine dispute.

diplomacy.terms: Messana asks Carthage to protect its safety and self-rule against a Syracusan attack while our discussions with Syracuse continue. We seek immediate assurances and aid sufficient to deter an assault; this request does not surrender our local laws or self-government.
diplomacy.subject: Protection for Messana while talks continue
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage will not send troops while its consultation with Syracuse proceeds. We will continue to press for notice and a peaceful hearing, but cannot promise protection by force.

diplomacy.terms: I send an envoy to present Messana's case. Hear our claim to self-rule and the safety of its inhabitants before deciding the city's future. We will discuss practical safeguards, but Messana's laws and people must be heard.
diplomacy.subject: Envoy for Messana's case
diplomacy.answerText: I will hear Messana’s case and its proposed safeguards. Send your envoy; the city’s safety and laws will be heard before I decide its future.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage proposes that Syracuse give notice before any action affecting Messana, the strait, or Carthaginian western possessions. Our envoys should meet promptly to settle the form of notice and the time allowed for consultation. This consultation does not transfer Messana's local government to either power.
diplomacy.subject: Notice and consultation at Messana
diplomacy.answerText: I accept prompt advance notice and consultation before action affecting Messana, the strait, or your western possessions. Our envoys will settle the form and time allowed; this does not determine Messana’s local government.

diplomacy.terms: I welcome your envoy. Let our representatives settle prompt advance notice and a meeting before any action at Messana that may affect the strait or Carthage’s western possessions. This consultation need not determine Syracuse’s claim against Messana.
diplomacy.subject: Scope and timing of consultation
diplomacy.answerText: Agreed. Our representatives will settle prompt notice and a meeting before any action affecting the strait or Carthage’s western possessions. This consultation does not determine Syracuse’s claim against Messana.

diplomacy.terms: I ask Rome to state the judgment to be imposed on the delivered men and how their ten-year punitive service is to be administered. Fix their duties, command, and provision plainly, so they know what they must endure.
diplomacy.subject: Judgment and service terms for the Rhegian garrison
diplomacy.answerText: Rome will administer the ten-year punitive service under Roman command, on assigned duties with ordinary provision, as already stated. Rome will take possession of Rhegium under the accepted peace terms.

diplomacy.terms: Messana seeks Roman protection against a Syracusan attack. We ask Rome to deter Syracuse and preserve the city’s self-rule; we are prepared to discuss terms promptly.
diplomacy.subject: Protection for Messana’s self-rule
diplomacy.answerText: Very well we shall send Legio I to defend you

diplomacy.terms: Let our envoys settle prompt notice and a meeting before any Syracusan action at Messana affecting the strait or Carthaginian western possessions. Such consultation shall not decide Syracuse’s claim against Messana.
diplomacy.subject: Consultation before action at Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Agreed. Our representatives will settle prompt notice and a meeting before any action affecting the strait or Carthaginian western possessions. This consultation does not determine Syracuse’s claim against Messana.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage again requests advance notice and a prompt consultation before any action affecting Messana, the strait, or Carthaginian western possessions. This request concerns consultation and does not commit Carthage to war or intervention.
diplomacy.subject: Renewed request for consultation before action
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse will give advance notice and meet promptly before action affecting Messana, the strait, or Carthaginian western possessions. Consultation does not determine our claim against Messana.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage proposes that Syracuse give prompt advance notice of any intended action affecting Messana, the strait, or Carthage’s western possessions. Within five days of notice, the parties’ representatives should meet to consult; consultation should conclude within ten days, after which Syracuse may act. This procedure does not decide Messana’s local government or Syracuse’s claim. Please appoint an envoy empowered to settle the procedure.
diplomacy.subject: Notice and consultation procedure at Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse accepts prompt advance notice and consultation before action affecting Messana, the strait, or Carthaginian western possessions. This leaves Messana's government and Syracuse's claim undecided.

diplomacy.terms: I propose immediate notice of any planned Syracusan action affecting Messana, the strait, or your western possessions, followed by a consultation meeting within five days before action proceeds. This procedure does not determine Syracuse’s claim against Messana.
diplomacy.subject: Notice and consultation at Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage accepts immediate notice and a meeting within five days before action affecting Messana, the strait, or our western possessions. Consultation shall not decide Syracuse’s claim.

diplomacy.terms: The Mamertines ask Carthage to deter a Syracusan attack and consult with Messana on its defense. They offer access to the harbor and a voice in decisions affecting the strait, while seeking to retain their local laws and self-rule. This appeal is not a surrender of the city.
diplomacy.subject: Protection and consultation for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage will not undertake military protection of Messana. We will remain neutral while consulting with Syracuse over actions affecting the strait.

diplomacy.terms: Syracuse will give Carthage advance notice of planned action at Messana affecting the strait or Carthaginian western possessions. Our representatives will meet within five days of notice; consultation will conclude within ten days. This procedure does not decide Syracuse's claim against Messana.
diplomacy.subject: Notice and consultation procedure
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage accepts advance notice, a meeting within five days, and conclusion of consultation within ten days. This does not commit Carthage to intervention or determine Syracuse’s claim.

diplomacy.terms: Messana renews its request for Roman protection against a Syracusan attack. We seek prompt discussion of terms that will deter Syracuse while preserving Messana’s self-rule. Please answer whether Rome will protect us and what terms it requires.
diplomacy.subject: Protection and terms for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Rome will discuss protection promptly, but I cannot pledge Roman protection without terms. Messana must accept Roman consultation on measures affecting its defence and the strait; in return, Rome will hear its claim to self-rule and seek to deter a Syracusan attack.

diplomacy.terms: Messana has appealed separately for Carthaginian protection and consultation over its defense. Rome has accepted our request for protection, but we still seek your answer. We ask Carthage to state promptly whether it will help preserve Messana's safety and self-rule.
diplomacy.subject: Answer Messana's appeal
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage declines military protection. Our neutrality and the consultation procedure with Syracuse remain in force.

diplomacy.terms: Rome has accepted responsibility to protect Messana. Send a clear account of what aid Rome will provide and when it will arrive. Messana seeks protection while retaining its self-rule; Syracuse threatens the city directly.
diplomacy.subject: Concrete protection for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: No answer came.

diplomacy.terms: Give Messana notice of any proposed action affecting the city or the strait, and consult Messana and Carthage before acting. This procedure must preserve Messana's safety and self-rule.
diplomacy.subject: Notice and consultation before action affecting Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse will give advance notice to Carthage and consult it under our agreed procedure. I will hear Messana’s terms, but cannot promise that consultation with Messana will preserve its self-rule or suspend Syracuse’s claim. I invite Mettius to meet promptly.

diplomacy.terms: Rome demands that Syracuse cease its hostilities against Messana. Continued attacks will be treated as an invitation to open war. Rome has undertaken to protect Messana; this warning does not waive the city's self-rule or its right to be heard.
diplomacy.subject: Cease hostilities against Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse will maintain its present pause and hear Messana’s terms. I cannot accept Rome’s demand as a renunciation of our claim or of our right to negotiate.

diplomacy.terms: I invite you to set out the practical arrangements Rome has offered Messana, including how its self-rule is to be safeguarded. Syracuse’s claim remains, and this inquiry is not a suspension of it.
diplomacy.subject: Practical terms for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Rome has been asked for practical protection arrangements, but I have no terms from Rome to set before you. I will discuss Messana’s self-rule directly: let Syracusan advances pause while we negotiate, without prejudice to your claim.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage stands by our agreed advance notice and consultation procedure. Please send notice before any action affecting Messana, the strait, or our western possessions; consultation does not itself commit Carthage to intervention.
diplomacy.subject: Consultation procedure remains in force
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse will give the advance notice we agreed. Consultation does not bind Carthage to intervene.

diplomacy.terms: Meet me within five days to discuss a temporary suspension of Syracusan advances and practical terms for Messana. Syracuse reserves its claim; I will hear proposals that protect the city's inhabitants and avert a wider war.
diplomacy.subject: Terms for a meeting on Messana
diplomacy.answerText: I will meet within five days. Messana's safety and self-rule must be heard; let the pause in advances hold while we negotiate.

diplomacy.terms: I will meet within five days. Let Syracusan advances pause while we speak. Messana will discuss practical terms only if its self-rule and the safety of its people are taken seriously.
diplomacy.subject: A meeting on Messana’s terms
diplomacy.answerText: I will meet you and keep the pause in advances while we negotiate. Messana’s safety and self-rule will be heard, though Syracuse reserves its claim.

diplomacy.terms: Under our agreed procedure, Syracuse gives advance notice that it is considering action affecting Messana. I request the consultation meeting within five days and will conclude consultation within ten. This notice does not suspend Syracuse’s claim.
diplomacy.subject: Notice and consultation before action at Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage will meet within five days and conclude consultation within ten. This procedure does not bind Carthage to intervene.

diplomacy.terms: Rome has been asked for practical protection arrangements, but I have no terms from Rome to set before you. I will discuss Messana’s self-rule directly: let Syracusan advances pause while we negotiate, without prejudice to your claim. I will meet you within the agreed five days.
diplomacy.subject: Rome’s answer and the terms for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: I will meet you within the agreed time and keep the pause while we discuss practical terms. Syracuse reserves its claim; Messana’s safety and self-rule will be heard.

diplomacy.terms: Rome has not answered Messana's request for protection, and Syracuse's threat remains. We renew our appeal for Carthaginian protection or aid to deter an attack, while seeking to preserve Messana's self-rule. Please answer promptly; we are prepared to discuss practical terms.
diplomacy.subject: Renewed appeal for protection of Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage will discuss practical guarantees for Messana, but will not promise military protection or intervention. Your appeal does not alter Carthage’s neutrality.

diplomacy.terms: I will meet as agreed. Messana's safety and self-rule must be addressed, and the pause in advances must hold while we negotiate. State what Syracuse requires and what guarantees it will offer.
diplomacy.subject: Terms for our meeting
diplomacy.answerText: I will state Syracuse’s requirements plainly: the claim remains ours, but the pause holds while we negotiate. We will hear Messana’s safety and self-rule and discuss guarantees against attack during the talks.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage will not undertake military protection of Messana. We remain neutral, but invite you to state the terms you seek for consultation over any action affecting the strait or Carthaginian interests. This procedure does not bind Carthage to intervene.
diplomacy.subject: Terms for Carthaginian consultation
diplomacy.answerText: I accept your invitation to state the terms we seek for consultation. Carthage's refusal of military protection leaves Messana exposed; consultation must at least give us prompt notice and a hearing before action affecting the strait or our city.

diplomacy.terms: Rome will maintain its protection of Messana against Syracusan attack. We seek no transfer of the city's government: the Mamertines may continue their self-rule while Roman forces defend the position at the strait. We will discuss practical arrangements with your representatives.
diplomacy.subject: Rome’s protection of Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Messana accepts Rome's protection against Syracusan attack on the understanding that our self-rule remains intact. We will meet your representatives to settle practical arrangements.

diplomacy.terms: Rome's forces have crossed to Messana, and war with Carthage has followed. Messana asks Rome to state promptly how it will protect the city and preserve its self-rule while the war continues. We seek practical terms that keep the fighting from consuming our homes.
diplomacy.subject: Security arrangements for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: No answer came.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage protests Rome's presence at the strait. Give advance notice and consult Carthage before further action affecting Messana, the strait, or Carthaginian western interests. This demand does not constitute a promise of Carthaginian protection for Messana.
diplomacy.subject: Carthaginian protest over the strait

diplomacy.terms: Rome will discuss protection promptly, but I cannot pledge Roman protection without terms. Messana must accept Roman consultation on measures affecting its defence and the strait; in return, Rome will hear its claim to self-rule and seek to deter a Syracusan attack.
diplomacy.subject: Rome's terms for discussing protection
diplomacy.answerText: Messana accepts consultation on measures affecting its defence and the strait while its final status remains open. We ask Rome to deter a Syracusan attack during these discussions and to state what practical protection it can provide.

diplomacy.terms: Messana asks Carthage to deter a Syracusan attack while preserving our self-rule. We seek prompt talks on practical protection and a clear consultation with Syracuse before any advance against the city. We will continue negotiations with Hieron during the present pause.
diplomacy.subject: Protection and consultation for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage will not promise armed protection now. We will press for immediate consultation with Syracuse and practical guarantees for Messana's self-rule while the pause holds.

diplomacy.terms: Messana can discuss Roman consultation on measures affecting its defence and the strait, but will not surrender its self-rule in advance. Will Rome offer protection against a Syracusan attack while these terms are discussed, and leave Messana’s final status open to agreement?
diplomacy.subject: Terms for protecting Messana
diplomacy.answerText: No answer came.

diplomacy.terms: I will receive you within three days. State Messana’s terms for safety and self-rule plainly; the pause in advances holds while we discuss them. Syracuse reserves its claim. I will observe the agreed consultation procedure with Carthage before any further action affecting the strait.
diplomacy.subject: Resume the Messana terms

diplomacy.terms: Messana asks Carthage to deter a Syracusan attack while talks continue. We seek protection that preserves our self-rule, not a transfer of our city. Please state promptly what aid or guarantees Carthage will offer.
diplomacy.subject: Protection for Messana during negotiations
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage will hear proposals for practical guarantees, but offers no military aid or promise to intervene. Messana’s request does not bind Carthage to protect the city.

diplomacy.terms: Syracuse will hear Messana’s requirements while the pause holds. Our claim remains; let us agree practical guarantees for the city’s safety during negotiations.
diplomacy.subject: Terms for Messana’s safety
diplomacy.answerText: No answer came.

diplomacy.terms: Messana remains exposed to Syracuse. We ask Carthage to state promptly whether it will deter an attack, and to hear terms that preserve our self-rule. We continue talks with Syracuse, but cannot treat silence as protection.
diplomacy.subject: A prompt answer on Messana’s protection
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage will not promise armed protection now. We will press for immediate consultation with Syracuse and practical guarantees for Messana's self-rule while the pause holds.

diplomacy.terms: I will meet to discuss practical guarantees for Messana’s safety and self-rule during the pause. We need terms that make the pause credible while these talks proceed.
diplomacy.subject: Practical terms for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: No answer came.

diplomacy.terms: I invite you to resume talks promptly. Syracuse’s claim remains reserved, but the pause in advances holds while we negotiate. State the guarantees Messana seeks for its safety and self-rule; we will discuss practical terms before any further action affecting Messana or the strait.
diplomacy.subject: Resume talks on Messana’s safety
diplomacy.answerText: No answer came.

diplomacy.terms: Messana renews its request for Carthaginian protection or other assurances able to deter a Syracusan attack during negotiations. We seek protection that preserves our self-rule. Please state promptly whether Carthage will offer such protection or what terms it requires.
diplomacy.subject: Prompt answer on protection for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage will not promise armed protection now. We will press for immediate consultation with Syracuse and practical guarantees for Messana's self-rule while the pause holds.

diplomacy.terms: I propose that we hold the agreed consultation at once. Syracuse will give advance notice before any further action affecting Messana or the strait; consultation will not itself bind Carthage to intervene.
diplomacy.subject: Consultation before action at Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Carthage accepts an immediate consultation under the agreed procedure. Syracuse must give advance notice before further action affecting Messana or the strait. Consultation does not commit Carthage to armed intervention.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage is ready to meet within the agreed period and conclude consultation within ten days. We will discuss notice of Syracusan action affecting the strait or our western interests; this procedure does not oblige Carthage to intervene.
diplomacy.subject: Agreed consultation on Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse accepts the meeting and the consultation procedure within the agreed period. Consultation on the matters named does not bind Carthage to intervene.

diplomacy.terms: We ask Carthage to state whether it will deter a Syracusan attack during negotiations. If it will not provide military protection, say so plainly and name any practical guarantee that could preserve Messana’s safety and self-rule.
diplomacy.subject: A clear answer on protection for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: No answer came.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage accepts immediate consultation. Let us record the scope and timing of notice before either side takes action affecting Messana, the strait, or western possessions. The current pause should hold while Messana's safety and self-rule are discussed.
diplomacy.subject: Immediate consultation on Messana and the strait
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse accepts immediate consultation and will observe the agreed notice procedure. The pause holds while Messana's safety and self-rule are discussed.

diplomacy.terms: Egypt asks Rome to take the safety of neutral shipping and open trade into account in its conduct of the wars around Messana. Egypt offers its good offices for discussions that might prevent the fighting from closing the ports.
diplomacy.subject: Keep the sea lanes open to commerce

diplomacy.terms: I invite you to resume talks promptly. Syracuse will discuss a pause in hostilities and practical guarantees for Messana’s safety and self-rule, while reserving its claim. I will consult Carthage before further action affecting Messana or the strait.
diplomacy.subject: Practical terms for Messana during the pause
diplomacy.answerText: I will resume talks promptly. Messana accepts a pause for these discussions, not a surrender of its self-rule. Put the practical guarantees in writing, and consult Carthage before further action affecting Messana or the strait.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage is prepared to hear what guarantees Messana seeks that do not require Carthaginian armed intervention. State your proposals promptly; we will continue to press for consultation with Syracuse while the pause holds.
diplomacy.subject: Hear Messana’s proposals for guarantees
diplomacy.answerText: Messana will offer its practical proposals promptly. We need written assurances that Syracuse will not attack during talks and that our self-rule will not be made a condition of them. Carthage must continue consultation with Syracuse and state how it will respond to a breach, though we do not demand an armed commitment now.

diplomacy.terms: The wars around Messana threaten the sea lanes on which Egyptian commerce depends. Keep the routes open and avoid measures that close the ports. Egypt offers its good offices to assist communication and reduce the danger of a wider conflict.
diplomacy.subject: Keep the sea lanes open; Egyptian good offices offered

diplomacy.terms: Messana is ready to continue talks. Confirm in writing that Syracusan forces will not advance against the city while negotiations continue, and that Messana’s self-rule will remain open to agreement. We will discuss practical terms promptly.
diplomacy.subject: Written guarantees during the pause
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse accepts a pause for these discussions. I will put the practical guarantees in writing: no advance against Messana while talks continue, Messana's self-rule remains open to agreement, and Carthage will be consulted before further action affecting Messana or the strait. Syracuse's claim is reserved.

diplomacy.terms: Syracuse proposes a temporary pause in advances while Messana’s safety and self-rule are discussed. Syracuse reserves its claim; we will consult Carthage before further action affecting the strait. Send your proposed guarantees in writing so we may settle terms.
diplomacy.subject: Written terms for a pause at Messana
diplomacy.answerText: Messana accepts the pause for talks and the written guarantees against advance while they continue. Our self-rule remains open to agreement, not surrendered; Syracuse reserves its claim, and Carthage is to be consulted before further action affecting Messana or the strait. We will continue talks promptly.

diplomacy.terms: Messana seeks a written guarantee that Syracusan advances will pause while talks proceed, and that the city’s self-rule will remain in force during them. State plainly what protection and restraint Syracuse will provide; our final status remains open to discussion.
diplomacy.subject: Written guarantees during the pause
diplomacy.answerText: Syracuse confirms the written guarantees already given: no advance against Messana while talks continue; Messana's self-rule remains open to agreement; and Carthage will be consulted before further action affecting Messana or the strait. Syracuse reserves its claim.

diplomacy.terms: Syracuse will maintain the present pause while talks proceed. Messana may govern itself during that pause, and its people and garrison will not be required to renounce their claim or submit to Syracuse as a condition of these talks. Syracuse reserves its claim and will consult Carthage before further action affecting Messana or the strait. I invite you to meet promptly to put practical guarantees in writing.
diplomacy.subject: Written guarantees during the pause
diplomacy.answerText: I accept the written assurance that Messana may govern itself during the pause and that this shall not be a condition of our talks. Messana reserves its own claim to govern itself. We will meet promptly to settle practical safeguards.

diplomacy.terms: Messana will resume talks promptly. Put in writing that Syracusan forces will not advance against the city while negotiations continue, that Messana's self-rule remains open to agreement, and that Carthage is consulted before further action affecting Messana or the strait. These terms are not a surrender of our self-rule.
diplomacy.subject: Written guarantees for Messana during the pause
diplomacy.answerText: I confirm the written guarantees: no Syracusan advance while talks continue, Messana's self-rule remains open to agreement, and Syracuse reserves its claim. Let us meet promptly to settle practical terms.

diplomacy.terms: Syracusan forces will not advance against Messana while negotiations continue. Messana's self-rule remains open to agreement; Syracuse reserves its claim. Syracuse will consult Carthage before further action affecting Messana or the strait. Let us meet promptly to settle practical terms.
diplomacy.subject: Written interim guarantees for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: I accept the pause and the written assurance that our self-rule remains open to agreement, not a condition of these talks. Messana reserves its own claim to govern itself. We will meet promptly to settle practical safeguards.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage will not promise armed intervention. I will hear Messana's requested practical guarantees and continue pressing for consultation with Syracuse before further action affecting Messana or the strait. Send the terms you seek, and we will discuss what can be secured without binding Carthage to war.
diplomacy.subject: Practical guarantees and consultation for Messana
diplomacy.answerText: No answer came.

diplomacy.terms: Carthage will continue to press for Messana's safety and a peaceful hearing while remaining outside armed intervention for now. State the practical guarantees Messana requires to preserve its self-rule during talks with Syracuse. Carthage will maintain consultation with Syracuse before action affecting the strait; this letter does not promise military protection.
diplomacy.subject: Practical guarantees for Messana

diplomacy.terms: Carthage accepts your invitation to hold the agreed consultation promptly. We will discuss advance notice before further action affecting Messana or the strait. Consultation does not bind Carthage to military intervention.
diplomacy.subject: Prompt consultation on Messana and the strait

diplomacy.terms: Carthage will not promise armed protection for Messana. We remain ready to discuss practical guarantees that may preserve the city's safety and self-rule; state plainly which guarantees Messana can accept.
diplomacy.subject: Carthage's answer on protection for Messana

diplomacy.terms: Rome publicly proposes a ceasefire between Rome and Syracuse. Rome will continue to protect Messana against attack while respecting its self-rule and local laws. The parties should refrain from hostilities during talks. Refusal or silence will not be treated as permission for further Roman escalation.
diplomacy.subject: Public Roman proposal for a ceasefire at Messana

diplomacy.terms: Rome threatens Rhegium and its Campanian garrison. Carthage contests Rome's presence near the strait. Tell me what aid or common action Carthage can offer; I will hold Rhegium if my men can be supplied.
diplomacy.subject: Aid against Rome at the strait

diplomacy.terms: Messana seeks written confirmation that Syracuse will not advance against the city during negotiations and that Messana's self-rule remains open to agreement rather than surrender. We ask Carthage to continue consultation with Syracuse before action affecting the strait and to make clear what diplomatic response it will make if the pause is broken. We do not require Carthage to promise armed intervention.
diplomacy.subject: Practical guarantees for Messana

diplomacy.terms: I invite you to meet promptly to settle practical safeguards while the pause holds. Messana may govern itself during these talks; Syracuse reserves its claim. Let us agree how the pause and the safety of Messana's people and garrison will be maintained. I will give Carthage notice before any further action affecting Messana or the strait.
diplomacy.subject: Practical safeguards during the pause

diplomacy.terms: Syracuse confirms that the present pause will continue while talks proceed. Messana may govern itself during that pause; neither its people nor its garrison must renounce their claim or submit to Syracuse as a condition of these talks. Syracuse reserves its claim and will consult Carthage before further action affecting Messana or the strait. Let us meet promptly to settle practical safeguards.
diplomacy.subject: Written safeguards during the pause

diplomacy.terms: Syracuse maintains the pause while practical safeguards for Messana are discussed. We give advance notice of these terms and request the agreed consultation before any further action affecting Messana or the strait. Syracuse reserves its claim; the terms do not require Messana to surrender self-rule during talks.
diplomacy.subject: Consultation on Messana and the strait

diplomacy.terms: We are withing our right, Messena is our protectorate
diplomacy.subject: We are withing our right, Messena is our protectorate
